title: Slice restriction preserves finite colimits.
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category in universe $u$, with morphisms in the same universe, let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with values in universe $u$, and let $U\in\mathcal C$. Let $R$ be the underlying sheaf of rings of $\mathcal O$. Use the category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of sheaves of $R$-modules with values in universe $u$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,R|_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then sectionwise restriction $j_U^*: \operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R|_U)$, defined by $(j_U^*M)(V\to U)=M(V)$ and $(j_U^*f)_{V\to U}=f_V$, preserves finite colimits. Equivalently, for every finite indexing category $I$ and every diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, restriction takes each colimit cocone of $D$ to a colimit cocone of $D\mathbin{\circ}j_U^*$ (composition in application order).

proof.text: Let R be the underlying ring sheaf of O, F = SheafOfModules.overFunctor R U, T = SheafOfModules.toSheaf (R.over U), and H = J.overPullback AddCommGrpCat U. Over.forget U is continuous and cocontinuous by Mathlib Sites.Over. Mathlib Functor.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous makes H a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits of size u and hence finite colimits. This works for an arbitrary small site, without assuming products or pullbacks.

The proved source-library instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf, realizing the forgetful-colimit clause of lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful, makes module forgetting preserve finite colimits on both sites. F followed by T is definitionally the composite of module forgetting on the original site with H. Thus F followed by T preserves finite colimits.

T reflects isomorphisms, and finite colimits exist in its source and are preserved by T. Therefore reflectsColimitsOfShape_of_reflectsIsomorphisms supplies reflection of each finite colimit, assembled into ReflectsFiniteColimits T. Apply preservesFiniteColimits_of_reflects_of_preserves to F and T. This proves the original restriction functor preserves finite colimits, with no additional hypotheses.
